title: Join Our Contractor Network | Genstone Construction
metaDescription: Licensed and insured contractors: join Genstone's nationwide network for investor, rental, REO and residential renovation work with defined scopes and draws.
lede: Join a nationwide network of qualified contractors supporting residential renovation projects across the country. Genstone's project-management teams coordinate scopes, documentation, inspections, quality control and payments, so contractor partners can concentrate on doing quality work on the job site. In return, we ask partners to meet six standards that our investor and institutional clients depend on.

sections.body:
Genstone Construction renovates properties for real estate investors, mortgage servicers, REITs, investment funds, banks with REO inventory and other mortgage lenders, and is a preferred contractor for Government-Sponsored Enterprises. The work is performed in each market by vetted local contractors, and Genstone's team in Romeoville, Illinois, handles the scoping, client relationship, documentation and billing around it.

What that means for a contractor partner:

- Access to renovation project opportunities across Genstone's service footprint
- Dedicated project-management support
- Centralized scopes, work orders, documentation and communication
- A defined draw and payment process
- Ongoing opportunities across investor, rental, REO and other residential renovation work

The work varies from kitchen and bath renovations to rental turns, larger rehabs, additions and full-property renovations. Many of these clients own more than one property, and many have repeat work, which is why the standards below matter.

sections.h2: What working on a Genstone project looks like
sections.body:
A typical project starts with a defined scope. Genstone's estimators have already walked the property, priced the work and set out the labor, materials and draw schedule, so you aren't selling the client on the job or negotiating finishes with them. You review the scope and the opportunity, and in many cases decide whether to bid.

Once a project is assigned, a Genstone field manager or project manager is your counterpart for the life of the job. Work orders, documents and communication run through one place. Questions from the client go to your project manager, not to your phone at night. When you open a wall and find something nobody expected, you document it and send it up, and the change gets reviewed and approved with the client before you do the extra work, which is also how it gets paid.

Payments follow the approved scope and draw schedule. When a stage is complete and documented, it can be billed. You don't chase the client for money, and the client doesn't pay ahead of the work.

The properties vary. Some are occupied rentals that need a turn between tenants. Some are vacant bank-owned houses that have been closed up for a long time. Some are flips where the investor wants listing-ready finishes. Knowing which kind of job you're walking into, and what the client expects from it, is part of what your project manager provides.

Every Genstone contractor is licensed, insured and carefully vetted, then trained to deliver quality craftsmanship and a professional experience on every project. Our clients include institutions that report on every property they own, and investors who manage renovations from another city. Both depend on the contractor on site doing what the scope says, documenting it and keeping the project clean from a compliance standpoint. The six standards below are what we expect from every partner.

Contractors must hold every license required by the state and local jurisdictions where they work, and those requirements vary by location and by the type of work. Many jurisdictions require separate licensing for trades such as electrical, plumbing and HVAC, and contractor partners are responsible for making sure licensed trades perform that work. Insurance must meet Genstone's requirements before approval, and coverage needs to stay current for as long as you're in the network. Genstone verifies that contractors assigned to projects maintain appropriate insurance and applicable licensing, so expect to provide updated certificates when policies renew.

Our clients pay for professional, market-appropriate finishes matched to the property's intended use. A flip needs work that holds up to a buyer's inspection and looks right in listing photos. A rental needs work that survives tenants. In both cases the basics carry the job: level and straight installations, tight trim and caulk lines, properly sealed wet areas, clean paint lines, and a site left broom clean. Genstone provides a one-year workmanship warranty to clients, so work that has to be revisited costs everyone time. Doing it right the first time is the standard that keeps a partner getting more work.

Genstone coordinates required permits and inspections with contractor partners and the applicable building departments as part of the project-management process. Specific responsibilities can vary by project and jurisdiction. What doesn't vary is that permitted work gets inspected before it's covered. Unpermitted or uninspected work can block a client's sale, refinance or loan draw later, and that comes back to the project. Partners are expected to schedule work so inspections happen at the right stage, be present or available when the inspector needs access, and correct any items noted before moving on.

Many Genstone clients never visit the property during the renovation. Their lenders, asset managers and investors see the work through the documentation. That makes photos and records part of the deliverable, not an afterthought. Partners are expected to document conditions before work starts, at each significant stage, and at completion, with clear photos that show the work tied to each scope item. Hidden conditions discovered during demolition need to be photographed before anything is covered or repaired, so the change can be reviewed and approved. Good documentation is also what keeps draws moving.

Lien waivers are part of how Genstone protects clients' title and keeps the payment process clean. When you're paid for work, you provide a waiver for that work, and you're responsible for making sure the subcontractors and suppliers you use are paid and provide their waivers too. An unpaid sub or supplier can file a lien on the client's property, which can delay a sale or refinance and puts the relationship at risk. State-specific lien waiver forms are available to current partners through the Resources for Contractors page.

Investors pay interest, insurance, taxes and utilities every day a project is open, so schedules matter. Partners are expected to start when committed, staff the job to keep it moving, and communicate early when something threatens a milestone. The scope is the agreement. Work outside the scope, including upgrades a client asks you for directly, goes through Genstone's change process and gets approved and documented before it's performed. That protects the client's budget and makes sure you're paid for the extra work.

sections.h2: Who does well in the network
sections.body:
The contractors who get the most out of working with Genstone tend to have a few things in common. They run a real business, with licensing, insurance and paperwork kept current without being chased. They have a reliable crew or a set of subcontractors they trust, so they can staff a job when it's offered. They take photos as a habit rather than as a chore. They communicate early, including when the news isn't good. And they're comfortable working inside a defined scope, where the client's budget and the investor's numbers drive the decisions.

If that describes your company, the network can provide a steady source of renovation work alongside your own customers, without the sales and collections effort that comes with finding every job yourself.

Joining takes four steps.

- Review requirements. Read the Pre-Application Checklist and gather your documents: general contractor license, certificate of insurance, workers' compensation certificate or waiver, a completed current W-9 and a mutual non-disclosure agreement.
- Submit your application. Complete the online Contractor Application and upload your documents.
- Complete screening and onboarding. Genstone reviews your licensing, insurance, experience and compliance information, then walks approved partners through how scopes, documentation, draws and communication work.
- Receive project opportunities. Approved partners are presented with opportunities that match their location and capabilities, and in many cases can choose which ones to bid on.

Approval doesn't commit Genstone to a set number of assignments. Opportunities depend on market demand, project requirements, location and contractor qualifications.

sections.h2: Have questions about joining our network?
sections.body: The Contractor FAQs cover qualifications, project opportunities, permits, payments, subcontractors and more. For anything else, use the contact form and choose the contractor option, or call (312) 429-2637.
